title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and managers when initiating requests or evaluating compliance.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems, data, or procurement processes. Exceptions require documented approval (see Change Exceptions section).

Quick links
- Access request form: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-form
- Procurement playbook: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement-playbook
- Vendor security checklist: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-checklist
- Travel & expense submission: /confluence/finance-and-legal/travel-expenses

1) Access & permissions
Overview: Access is granted on the principle of least privilege. All elevated access (admin or production write) requires approval from the resource owner and the responsible security contact.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Resource owner (service/product team): approves role assignment for their service and periodically reviews memberships (quarterly).
- Eng-Infra: enforces IAM policies, maintains automation for RBAC groups.
- Security team: performs periodic audits and approves exceptions.
- People-ops: coordination for directory/group lifecycle and contractor on/offboarding.

Standard process to request access:
1. Submit an Access Request via the Access Request Form with: requested role, justification, duration (if temporary), and approver (resource owner).
2. Request auto-routed to resource owner -> security reviewer (if admin) -> eng-infra to provision.
3. Provisioning executed via automation; ticket closed with details and expiration date.

Temporary/Break-glass access:
- Temporary elevated access is limited to 8 hours by default and requires the on-call owner and a security reviewer to approve live. Break-glass events must be logged in the incident tracker and reviewed within 3 business days.

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly access review led by resource owners. Remediation actions must be completed within 10 business days.

2) Change management
Purpose: Ensure predictable, auditable, low-risk changes to production and shared infrastructure.

Change types and approvals:
- Standard Change: pre-approved, repeatable changes (patch windows, minor config updates). Requires change request logged; CAB approval not required but owner must notify stakeholders.
- Normal Change: non-emergency changes that require CAB review for production-impacting work. Submit at least 48 hours before the CAB meeting.
- Emergency Change: outage-driven changes. Implement immediately after notifying on-call and logging the change; CAB retrospective required within 48 hours.

Change advisory board (CAB):
- Members: Eng-Platform lead, Eng-SRE lead, Security, Product owner (affected area), and a Finance representative for cost-impactful changes.
- Weekly meeting: Wednesdays 10:00-11:00 UTC. Submit RFCs by Tuesday 17:00 UTC for inclusion.

Change window and blackout periods:
- Standard maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00-06:00 UTC for disruptive infra changes.
- Blackout periods: Money/earnings close, major launch windows; see product calendar for dates.

Rollback and post-change validation:
1. Define rollback plan in the RFC.
2. Perform smoke tests within 30 minutes of change completion.
3. If metric regressions exceed thresholds (latency +20% or error rate >2% absolute increase), invoke rollback.

3) Data management
Classification:
- Public: safe to release outside the company.
- Internal: company-internal but not sensitive.
- Confidential: contains customer data, PII, or proprietary model artifacts. Access restricted and logged.

Storage and retention:
- Logs: retained 90 days in hot storage, 2 years archival (compressed).
- Backups (customer data): daily incremental, weekly full; retention 7 years for financial/legal requirements where applicable.
- Model artifacts and training data: retention policy defined per team; default is 3 years unless otherwise classified.

Data access requests and approvals:
1. Submit Data Access Request with dataset identifier, purpose, and intended use.
2. Data steward (owner) + Security approve for Confidential data.
3. Access is time-limited and requires review after 30/90/365 days depending on classification.

Data deletion and portability:
- Customer data deletion requests follow the Data Deletion Runbook: log request -> verify identity -> remove copies in primary and backup stores within 30 days unless legal hold applies.

Encryption and key management:
- All Confidential data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Key management must use the company KMS (cloud KMS or HSM for on-prem). Key rotation: annually or per security request.

Audit and compliance:
- Security performs quarterly audits on high-risk datasets. Findings produce an action plan with owners and target dates.

4) Procurement & expenses
Roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: submits purchase requests and manages vendor interactions until PO is issued.
- Finance: validates budgets, issues POs, processes invoices and expense reimbursements.
- Legal: supports contract review for vendors exceeding $25,000 ARR or with data access requirements.

Thresholds and approval matrix (table):
- <$5,000: Manager approval (email + procurement form).
- $5,000- $25,000: Director approval + finance review.
- >$25,000: VP approval + legal & finance involvement; procurement lead creates PO and negotiates SLA.

Procurement steps (standard):
1. Complete Procurement Request form with justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Finance validates budget and issues a PO if approved.
3. Legal reviews if contract terms require it (see thresholds above).
4. Vendor onboarding (security questionnaire) before giving access to Confidential data.

Expenses and travel reimbursement:
- Submit expenses within 30 days of spend with receipts via the expense system.
- Per diem and caps: domestic meals $75/day, international higher depending on region; air travel must be economy for <6 hour flights, premium economy for 6-10 hours, business for >10 hours with manager pre-approval. See Travel section for full rules.

5) Vendor management
Onboarding checklist:
1. Procurement request + budget approval.
2. Vendor security questionnaire completed.
3. Legal contract executed with data processing addendum if vendor accesses customer or confidential data.
4. Finance sets up vendor in AP system.

Risk tiers and controls:
- Tier 1 (high risk): Vendors processing Confidential data or with production access. Require SOC 2 type II or equivalent, penetration test within last 12 months, and a signed DPA.
- Tier 2 (medium risk): Business tools with no customer data. Require security questionnaire and annual review.
- Tier 3 (low risk): Marketing tools or one-off consultants with limited access. Require basic vendor form and finance approval.

SLA and monitoring:
- Standard SLA template: uptime 99.9% for core infra services, incident response time SLA 4 hours for P1 incidents. Custom SLAs negotiated for critical services.

Vendor offboarding:
- Revoke all credentials, remove from SSO groups, collect owned assets, and confirm data disposal per contract. Offboarding checklist must be completed within 5 business days of contract termination.

6) Travel policy (people-ops owned)
Booking and approvals:
- All work travel must be pre-approved in the travel system. Include trip purpose, itinerary, and budget code.
- Non-routine business class requires VP approval and documented business justification.

Allowed expenses and receipts:
- Airfare, lodging, ground transportation, meals, and reasonable incidentals.
- Itemized receipts required for all expenses >$25. Alcohol is reimbursable only when entertaining customers with manager approval.

Safety and emergency procedures:
- Register travel in the travel safety tool. For emergency evacuation assistance contact Security (security@redwood.example.com) and People Ops.

7) Internal templates and standard forms
Included templates (links):
- Access request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-form
- Procurement request template: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement-request
- Vendor security questionnaire: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-questionnaire
- Travel request & expense template: /confluence/finance-and-legal/travel-expense-template
- Change request/RFC template: /confluence/eng-platform/change-request-template

How to use templates:
- Fill required fields only; automated validations are enforced by the submission form. Provide concise business justification and include budget codes where applicable.

Exceptions and emergency processes
- Exceptions to these policies require a documented Exception Request form and explicit approval by the policy owner and Security/Finance as applicable. Emergency changes and access follow the emergency flows described above and require post-facto documentation and CAB review.

Governance and review cadence
- This document is reviewed annually by People Ops, Security, Finance, and Eng-Infra. Major changes require CAB review and publication notes.

Contacts and escalation
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security team: security@redwood.example.com
- Finance/Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Eng-Infra (IAM): infra-iam@redwood.example.com

Appendix A: Example forms and quick procedures
- Quick access provisioning (temporary) checklist: request -> owner approval -> security rapid review -> time-limited provisioning -> log entry.
- Emergency change checklist: notify on-call -> implement mitigation -> log incident -> postmortem & CAB retrospective within 48 hours.

Appendix B: Change and procurement SLA table
- CAB turnaround for Normal changes: 3 business days from submission for non-critical items.
- Procurement PO issuance: standard items 5-7 business days after approval; contracts with negotiations 10-30 business days.

Document history
- 2026-03-04: created (Jordan Patel).
- 2026-11-18: updated thresholds, added vendor tiering and travel clarifications (reviewers: Asha Kapoor, Miguel Alvarez, Samantha Li).

If you have questions or need a template exported as a fillable form, contact people-ops@redwood.example.com.
